best_for: Students, writers and researchers who think in outlines and want a free mind-map tool they can script and run from a USB stick.

points.title: Free, open source, no account
points.text: Freeplane is GPL software for mind mapping, notes and task lists. Nothing is behind a paywall and there is no sign-in.

points.title: Goes past plain mind maps
points.text: Conditional styles, formulas, command search and add-ons are built in, and Groovy scripts let you automate changes across a whole map.

points.title: Java matters on Windows and Linux
points.text: It is a Java app. The Windows with-Java installer and the macOS disk images include their own Java. The plain Windows setup needs Java 8 to 22 installed, and the Linux .deb and zip need Java 11 to 21.

points.title: Runs from a stick
points.text: A portable build can run from removable storage, so you can carry maps between computers without installing anything.

points.title: The Flatpak is a community build
points.text: Flathub does not mark the Flatpak as verified. It is published under Dimitry Polivaev's name, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Mac can trail Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 25 versions, with per-user and machine-wide installers. macOS lists only the current release here, which was 1.13.3 when Windows was on 1.13.5, so downgrades there need another source.
